name: Ehud
who: A Benjaminite, son of Bilhan, whose family was counted among Benjamin's mighty warriors.
key: The sons of Bilhan were Jeush, Benjamin, Ehud, Chenaanah, Zethan, Tarshish, and Ahishahar (1 Chronicles 7).
They were heads of fathers' houses, mighty warriors, 17,200 able to go to war (1 Chronicles 7).

name: Eker
who: A man of Judah, son of Ram, the firstborn of Jerahmeel, named in Chronicles' genealogy of Judah.
key: Eker was a son of Ram, the firstborn of Jerahmeel (1 Chronicles 2).
His brothers were Maaz and Jamin (1 Chronicles 2).

name: Elah
who: A king of Israel, son of Baasha, who reigned two years before Zimri assassinated him.
key: He became king at Tirzah in Asa's twenty-sixth year and reigned two years (1 Kings 16).
While he was drunk in his steward's house, his commander Zimri struck him down (1 Kings 16).

name: Elah
who: The father of Hoshea, the last king of the northern kingdom of Israel.
key: His son Hoshea conspired against King Pekah, killed him, and became king (2 Kings 15).
Hoshea son of Elah reigned nine years in Samaria until Assyria captured it (2 Kings 17).

name: Elah
who: A son of Caleb son of Jephunneh and father of Kenaz, named in the genealogy of Judah.
key: Caleb son of Jephunneh had three sons: Iru, Elah, and Naam (1 Chronicles 4).
The son of Elah was Kenaz (1 Chronicles 4).

name: Elam
who: The ancestor of a large family whose descendants returned to Judah after the exile.
key: His descendants, 1,254 in all, returned with Zerubbabel (Ezra 2).
More of his descendants came up from Babylon with Ezra (Ezra 8).

name: Eldaah
who: A son of Midian and grandson of Abraham through Keturah.
key: He is listed among the sons of Midian, son of Abraham and Keturah (Genesis 25).
Chronicles repeats him among Keturah's descendants (1 Chronicles 1).

name: Eldad
who: One of the seventy elders of Israel who prophesied in the camp in Moses' day.
key: He was registered among the seventy elders but remained in the camp (Numbers 11).
The Spirit rested on him and Medad, and they prophesied in the camp (Numbers 11).

name: Elead
who: A son of Ephraim, killed with Ezer by the men of Gath while raiding their livestock.
key: Ezer and Elead were killed by the men of Gath when they came down to take their livestock (1 Chronicles 7).
Ephraim their father mourned many days, and his brothers came to comfort him (1 Chronicles 7).

name: Eleazar
who: Son of Aaron who succeeded his father as Israel's high priest.
key: He was placed over the leaders of the Levites and the care of the sanctuary (Numbers 3).
On Mount Hor, Aaron's priestly garments were put on him before Aaron died (Numbers 20).

name: Eleazar
who: Son of Dodo the Ahohite and one of the three chief warriors among David's mighty men.
key: He is named second among the three chief mighty men of David (2 Samuel 23).
He struck down Philistines until his hand clung to his sword, and the LORD brought a great victory (2 Samuel 23).

name: Eleazar
who: A Levite of the clan of Merari, son of Mahli, who died leaving daughters but no sons.
key: He is listed among the Merarite Levites as a son of Mahli and brother of Kish (1 Chronicles 23).
He died without sons, and his daughters married their cousins, the sons of Kish (1 Chronicles 23).

name: Eleazar
who: Son of Phinehas who helped receive and weigh the temple treasures Ezra brought to Jerusalem.
key: After Ezra's company reached Jerusalem, he joined Meremoth the priest in weighing the silver, gold, and vessels (Ezra 8).
Everything was counted and recorded, and the returned exiles offered burnt offerings to God (Ezra 8).

name: Elhanan
who: A warrior of David from Bethlehem who killed Lahmi, the brother of Goliath.
key: During David's wars with the Philistines, he fought in a battle at Gob (2 Samuel 21).
He struck down Lahmi, the brother of Goliath, whose spear shaft was like a weaver's beam (1 Chronicles 20).

name: Eli
who: The priest at Shiloh who judged Israel forty years and raised the young Samuel.
key: Eli mistook Hannah's silent prayer for drunkenness, then blessed her (1 Samuel 1).
A man of God announced judgment because Eli honored his wicked sons above God (1 Samuel 2).

name: Eliab
who: A son of Helon who served as the leader of the tribe of Zebulun in the wilderness.
key: He was appointed to help Moses take the census for Zebulun (Numbers 1).
He led Zebulun's camp on the east side of the tabernacle (Numbers 2).

name: Eliab
who: A Reubenite, son of Pallu, and father of Dathan and Abiram, who rebelled against Moses.
key: His sons Dathan and Abiram joined Korah's rebellion against Moses (Numbers 16).
His sons Nemuel, Dathan, and Abiram are listed among Reuben's clans (Numbers 26).

name: Eliab
who: The eldest son of Jesse and older brother of King David.
key: Samuel thought he was the Lord's anointed, but the Lord looks on the heart (1 Samuel 16).
He served in Saul's army facing the Philistines (1 Samuel 17).

name: Eliada
who: Father of Rezon, the Syrian leader who seized Damascus and became an adversary of Solomon.
key: God raised up Rezon son of Eliada as an adversary to Solomon (1 Kings 11).
Rezon had fled from his master Hadadezer king of Zobah and gathered a band of men (1 Kings 11).

name: Eliakim
who: Son of Hilkiah, royal household administrator for King Hezekiah during the Assyrian threat.
key: Isaiah foretold that God would place Eliakim over the royal household in place of Shebna (Isaiah 22).
He went out to meet the Rabshakeh and asked him to speak Aramaic, not Hebrew (2 Kings 18).

name: Eliasaph
who: The son of Deuel and chief of the tribe of Gad in the wilderness.
key: Named chief of the tribe of Gad to help Moses take the census (Numbers 1).
Led the army of Gad in its assigned place around the tabernacle (Numbers 2).

name: Eliashib
who: A descendant of David's royal line after the exile, one of the seven sons of Elioenai.
key: The sons of Elioenai were Hodaviah, Eliashib, Pelaiah, Akkub, Johanan, Delaiah, and Anani, seven (1 Chronicles 3).
His family belonged to the royal line of Zerubbabel and King Jehoiachin (1 Chronicles 3).

name: Eliashib
who: High priest in Nehemiah's day who led the priests in rebuilding Jerusalem's Sheep Gate.
key: He and his fellow priests rebuilt and consecrated the Sheep Gate and the nearby wall (Nehemiah 3).
Other builders repaired sections of the wall beside his house (Nehemiah 3).

name: Eliashib
who: High priest after the exile, grandson of Jeshua, who served while Nehemiah rebuilt Jerusalem.
key: He led the priests in rebuilding and consecrating the Sheep Gate of Jerusalem's wall (Nehemiah 3).
He is listed in the high priestly line as son of Joiakim and father of Joiada (Nehemiah 12).

name: Eliashib
who: A priest in charge of the temple storerooms who was related to Tobiah and gave him a room there.
key: Appointed over the temple chambers, he prepared a large storeroom for his relative Tobiah (Nehemiah 13).
That room had held the grain offerings, frankincense, vessels, and tithes for the Levites and priests (Nehemiah 13).

name: Eliel
who: Chief of the Levite clan of Hebron who helped bring the ark to Jerusalem under David.
key: As chief of Hebron's descendants, he led eighty of his relatives in David's service (1 Chronicles 15).
David told him and the other Levite leaders to consecrate themselves and bring up the ark (1 Chronicles 15).

name: Eliezer
who: The second son of Moses and Zipporah, whose descendants served among the Levites over the temple treasuries.
key: Jethro brought Zipporah and her two sons, Gershom and Eliezer, to Moses in the wilderness (Exodus 18).
Moses named him Eliezer, saying the God of his father had been his help (Exodus 18).

name: Eliezer
who: A prophet from Mareshah, son of Dodavahu, who rebuked King Jehoshaphat's alliance with Ahaziah of Israel.
key: He prophesied that the LORD would destroy Jehoshaphat's ships because he had joined with Ahaziah (2 Chronicles 20).
The ships built at Ezion-geber were wrecked and never sailed to Tarshish (2 Chronicles 20).

name: Elihu
who: A young man, son of Barachel the Buzite, who spoke after Job and his three friends fell silent.
key: Angry at Job and his three friends, he waited for his elders before speaking (Job 32).
He insisted that God does not act wickedly or pervert justice (Job 34).

name: Elijah
who: Prophet from Tishbe who confronted King Ahab and Baal worship in Israel and was taken up to heaven.
key: He announced a drought, was fed by ravens, and raised a widow's son (1 Kings 17).
On Mount Carmel, God answered his prayer with fire, defeating the prophets of Baal (1 Kings 18).

name: Elika
who: A man of Harod, listed among David's thirty mighty men.
key: Shammah of Harod and Elika of Harod are listed among the thirty (2 Samuel 23).
The thirty also included Asahel the brother of Joab and Elhanan son of Dodo of Bethlehem (2 Samuel 23).

name: Elimelech
who: An Ephrathite of Bethlehem, husband of Naomi, who moved his family to Moab during a famine.
key: During a famine he took Naomi and their two sons from Bethlehem to Moab (Ruth 1).
He died in Moab, leaving Naomi with her two sons (Ruth 1).

name: Elioenai
who: A descendant of David's royal line after the exile, son of Neariah and father of seven sons.
key: He is listed as a son of Neariah, with his brothers Hizkiah and Azrikam (1 Chronicles 3).
His seven sons are named, including Hodaviah, Eliashib, Johanan, and Anani (1 Chronicles 3).

name: Eliphaz
who: Firstborn son of Esau by Adah, whose descendants became chiefs of Edom.
key: Adah bore Eliphaz to Esau in Canaan (Genesis 36).
His sons were Teman, Omar, Zepho, Gatam, and Kenaz (Genesis 36).

name: Eliphaz
who: Eliphaz the Temanite, one of the three friends who came to comfort Job.
key: He came with Bildad and Zophar to comfort Job and sat silently seven days (Job 2).
Speaking first, he argued that the innocent do not perish (Job 4).

name: Eliphelet
who: Son of Ahasbai of Maacah, one of David's thirty mighty men.
key: He is listed among the thirty, David's renowned mighty men (2 Samuel 23).
The list identifies him as the son of Ahasbai of Maacah (2 Samuel 23).

name: Elizabeth
who: Wife of the priest Zechariah and relative of Mary, who bore John the Baptist in old age.
key: A righteous descendant of Aaron, she was barren and advanced in years (Luke 1).
After conceiving, she kept herself hidden for five months (Luke 1).

name: Elisha
who: Son of Shaphat, Elijah's successor as prophet in Israel, known for many miracles.
key: Elijah threw his cloak on Elisha while he was plowing, and he followed him (1 Kings 19).
He received a double portion of Elijah's spirit when Elijah was taken up (2 Kings 2).

name: Elishah
who: A son of Javan and grandson of Japheth, listed in the table of nations after the flood.
key: He is listed as a son of Javan, the son of Japheth (Genesis 10).
From Javan's descendants the coastland peoples spread out into their lands (Genesis 10).

name: Elishama
who: A son of Ammihud who led the tribe of Ephraim in the wilderness, and grandfather of Joshua.
key: He was appointed to help Moses take the census for Ephraim (Numbers 1).
He led Ephraim's camp on the west side of the tabernacle (Numbers 2).

name: Elishama
who: A man of Judah's royal family, grandfather of Ishmael who assassinated the governor Gedaliah.
key: He is named as the father of Nethaniah, of the royal family (2 Kings 25).
His grandson Ishmael murdered Gedaliah, the governor Babylon had appointed over Judah (Jeremiah 41).

name: Elisheba
who: Daughter of Amminadab of Judah and sister of Nahshon, who became the wife of Aaron.
key: She married Aaron, the brother of Moses (Exodus 6).
She bore Aaron four sons: Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar (Exodus 6).

name: Elizaphan
who: A Levite, son of Uzziel, and chief of the Kohathite clans.
key: He is listed among the sons of Uzziel (Exodus 6).
Moses had him and Mishael carry the bodies of Nadab and Abihu out of the camp (Leviticus 10).

name: Elizur
who: The son of Shedeur and chief of the tribe of Reuben in the wilderness.
key: Named chief of the tribe of Reuben to help Moses take the census (Numbers 1).
Led the army of Reuben in its assigned place around the tabernacle (Numbers 2).

name: Elkanah
who: An Ephraimite of Ramathaim-zophim, husband of Hannah and Peninnah, and father of the prophet Samuel.
key: He went up yearly to worship at Shiloh and gave Hannah a double portion (1 Samuel 1).
He comforted Hannah in her grief and agreed to her vow concerning Samuel (1 Samuel 1).

name: Elon
who: A Hittite whose daughter married Esau, to the grief of Isaac and Rebekah.
key: Esau married his daughter, and the marriage made life bitter for Isaac and Rebekah (Genesis 26).
His daughter Adah is listed among Esau's wives as the mother of Eliphaz (Genesis 36).

name: Elon
who: A judge from the tribe of Zebulun who led Israel for ten years.
key: After Ibzan, Elon the Zebulunite judged Israel for ten years (Judges 12).
He died and was buried at Aijalon in the land of Zebulun (Judges 12).

name: Elymas
who: A Jewish magician and false prophet on Cyprus, struck blind for opposing the gospel before the proconsul.
key: Bar-Jesus, a Jewish false prophet and magician, was with the proconsul Sergius Paulus (Acts 13).
Elymas opposed Barnabas and Saul, seeking to turn the proconsul away from the faith (Acts 13).

name: Enan
who: A man of the tribe of Naphtali, the father of Ahira, Naphtali's chief in the wilderness.
key: He is named as the father of Ahira, chief of Naphtali, at the census (Numbers 1).
His son Ahira led Naphtali's army north of the tabernacle (Numbers 2).

name: Enoch
who: The firstborn son of Cain, after whom Cain named the city he built.
key: Born to Cain and his wife, he gave his name to the city Cain built (Genesis 4).
He became the father of Irad, continuing Cain's line down to Lamech (Genesis 4).

name: Enoch
who: A descendant of Seth, son of Jared, who walked with God and was taken by God without dying.
key: He fathered Methuselah, walked with God, and was no more, for God took him (Genesis 5).
He is listed in the line from Adam to Noah (1 Chronicles 1).

name: Enosh
who: Son of Seth and grandson of Adam, in whose days people began to call on the LORD's name.
key: After Seth's son Enosh was born, people began to call on the LORD's name (Genesis 4).
He fathered Kenan at ninety and lived 905 years in all (Genesis 5).

name: Epaphras
who: A believer from Colossae and fellow servant of Paul who taught the Colossians the gospel and labored for them in prayer.
key: The Colossians learned the gospel from Epaphras, a beloved fellow servant and faithful minister of Christ (Colossians 1).
He told Paul of the Colossians' love in the Spirit (Colossians 1).

name: Epaphroditus
who: A believer from Philippi whom Paul called his brother, fellow worker, and fellow soldier.
key: The Philippian church sent him as their messenger to minister to Paul's needs (Philippians 2).
He delivered the Philippians' gifts, which Paul called a fragrant offering pleasing to God (Philippians 4).

name: Ephah
who: A son of Midian and grandson of Abraham through Keturah, ancestor of an Arabian people.
key: He is listed first among the sons of Midian, Abraham's son by Keturah (Genesis 25).
He is named again among Midian's sons in the genealogies of Chronicles (1 Chronicles 1).

name: Ephah
who: A concubine of Caleb listed in the genealogy of the tribe of Judah.
key: She is named as a concubine of Caleb in Judah's family records (1 Chronicles 2).
She bore him Haran, Moza, and Gazez (1 Chronicles 2).

name: Ephah
who: A son of Jahdai listed in the genealogy of Caleb's clan in the tribe of Judah.
key: He is named among the six sons of Jahdai (1 Chronicles 2).
His family appears within the descendants of Caleb in Judah's genealogy (1 Chronicles 2).

name: Epher
who: A son of Midian and grandson of Abraham through Keturah.
key: He is listed among the sons of Midian, Abraham's son by Keturah (Genesis 25).
He is named again among Midian's sons in the genealogies of Chronicles (1 Chronicles 1).

name: Ephraim
who: Younger son of Joseph born in Egypt, ancestor of the tribe of Ephraim, a leading northern tribe.
key: Joseph named him Ephraim because God had made him fruitful in Egypt (Genesis 41).
Jacob crossed his hands and blessed Ephraim above his older brother Manasseh (Genesis 48).

name: Ephrathah
who: A wife of Caleb son of Hezron and mother of Hur, from whose line came the founder of Bethlehem.
key: After Azubah died, Caleb married Ephrath, who bore him Hur (1 Chronicles 2).
The sons of Hur, her firstborn, included Salma the father of Bethlehem (1 Chronicles 2).

name: Ephron
who: A Hittite, son of Zohar, who sold Abraham the field and cave of Machpelah as a family tomb.
key: He sold Abraham the field and cave of Machpelah for four hundred shekels of silver (Genesis 23).
Isaac and Ishmael buried Abraham in the cave in Ephron's former field (Genesis 25).

name: Er
who: The firstborn son of Judah, whom the Lord put to death for his wickedness.
key: He was born to Judah and the daughter of Shua (Genesis 38).
Judah took Tamar as his wife (Genesis 38).

name: Erastus
who: A helper of Paul who traveled with Timothy into Macedonia and later remained at Corinth.
key: From Ephesus, Paul sent him and Timothy ahead into Macedonia (Acts 19).
Erastus, the city treasurer, sent greetings with Paul to the believers in Rome (Romans 16).

name: Esau
who: Older twin brother of Jacob, son of Isaac and Rebekah, and ancestor of the Edomites.
key: Born first of twins, he later sold his birthright to Jacob for a meal (Genesis 25).
Jacob received Isaac's blessing instead of him, and Esau planned to kill Jacob (Genesis 27).

name: Eshban
who: A Horite, son of Dishon, among the clans of Seir who lived in the land before Esau's descendants.
key: The sons of Dishon were Hemdan, Eshban, Ithran, and Cheran (Genesis 36).
Chronicles repeats these sons of Dishon among the descendants of Seir (1 Chronicles 1).

name: Eshcol
who: An Amorite near Hebron, brother of Mamre and Aner, and an ally of Abram.
key: Eshcol and his brothers Mamre and Aner were allies of Abram (Genesis 14).
They went with Abram when he pursued the eastern kings to rescue Lot (Genesis 14).

name: Esther
who: Jewish orphan raised by Mordecai who became queen of Persia and saved her people from destruction.
key: Raised by her cousin Mordecai, she was chosen queen by King Ahasuerus (Esther 2).
Learning of Haman's plot, she asked the Jews to fast before she approached the king (Esther 4).

name: Ethan
who: A famous wise man called the Ezrahite, whose wisdom Solomon surpassed; Psalm 89 bears his name.
key: Solomon's wisdom surpassed that of Ethan the Ezrahite and the other renowned wise men of his day (1 Kings 4).
Psalm 89, a maskil of Ethan the Ezrahite, celebrates the LORD's steadfast love and covenant with David (Psalms 89).

name: Ethan
who: A Levite singer of the clan of Merari, appointed with Heman and Asaph to lead music under David.
key: Ethan son of Kishi stood at Heman's left among the singers David appointed (1 Chronicles 6).
The Levites appointed him with Heman and Asaph when David brought up the ark (1 Chronicles 15).

name: Eunice
who: The Jewish believing mother of Timothy and daughter of Lois, known for her sincere faith.
key: Timothy's mother was a Jewish believer, though his father was a Greek (Acts 16).
Paul recalled the sincere faith that lived first in Lois, then Eunice, and now Timothy (2 Timothy 1).

name: Eutychus
who: A young man at Troas who fell from a window during Paul's sermon and was restored to life.
key: During Paul's long talk late into the night at Troas, he sank into deep sleep in a window (Acts 20).
He fell from the third story and was taken up dead (Acts 20).

name: Eve
who: The first woman, made by God from Adam's rib, wife of Adam and mother of all the living.
key: God made her from the man's rib and brought her to Adam as his partner (Genesis 2).
Deceived by the serpent, she ate the forbidden fruit and gave some to Adam (Genesis 3).

name: Evil-merodach
who: A king of Babylon who released King Jehoiachin of Judah from prison.
key: In the year he began to reign, he released Jehoiachin from prison in the thirty-seventh year of exile (2 Kings 25).
He spoke kindly to Jehoiachin and gave him a seat above the other kings in Babylon (2 Kings 25).

name: Ezekiel
who: A priest, son of Buzi, taken into exile in Babylon and called there as God's prophet.
key: By the Chebar canal in Babylon, he saw visions of God's glory above a throne (Ezekiel 1).
God appointed him a watchman to warn the house of Israel (Ezekiel 3).

name: Ezer
who: A son of Seir the Horite and a Horite chief in Edom.
key: He is listed among the sons of Seir, inhabitants of the land (Genesis 36).
His sons Bilhan, Zaavan, and Akan are named, and he was a Horite chief (Genesis 36).

name: Ezer
who: A son of Ephraim, killed with his brother Elead by the men of Gath in a clash over livestock.
key: Ezer and Elead were killed by the native-born men of Gath in a livestock raid (1 Chronicles 7).
Their father Ephraim mourned many days, and his brothers came to comfort him (1 Chronicles 7).

name: Ezra
who: A priest and scribe skilled in the Law of Moses who led exiles from Babylon to Jerusalem.
key: With King Artaxerxes' letter, Ezra led a group from Babylon to Jerusalem (Ezra 7).
Grieved over intermarriage with the peoples, he prayed and led the people to repent (Ezra 9; Ezra 10).

name: Ezra
who: A priest and scribe skilled in the Law of Moses who led exiles home and taught God's Law in Jerusalem.
key: With the Persian king's letter, he led a company of exiles from Babylon to Jerusalem (Ezra 7).
Grieved that the people had intermarried with the peoples of the land, he prayed and confessed Israel's sin (Ezra 9).

name: Felix
who: Roman governor of Judea who heard Paul's case at Caesarea and kept him imprisoned two years.
key: The tribune Lysias sent Paul to Governor Felix at Caesarea with a letter (Acts 23).
He heard Tertullus accuse Paul and heard Paul's defense, then postponed a decision (Acts 24).

name: Fortunatus
who: A believer from Corinth who came to Paul with Stephanas and Achaicus and refreshed his spirit.
key: Paul rejoiced at the coming of Stephanas, Fortunatus, and Achaicus from Corinth (1 Corinthians 16).
They made up for the Corinthians' absence and refreshed Paul's spirit (1 Corinthians 16).

name: Gaal
who: Son of Ebed, who stirred Shechem to revolt against Abimelech and was defeated and driven out.
key: He moved into Shechem with his relatives, and its leaders put their trust in him (Judges 9).
At a festival he boasted he would remove Abimelech if the people were under him (Judges 9).

name: Gabriel
who: An angel who stands in God's presence and was sent with messages to Daniel, Zechariah, and Mary.
key: He explained to Daniel the vision of the ram and the goat (Daniel 8).
While Daniel was praying, Gabriel came swiftly and revealed the seventy weeks (Daniel 9).

name: Gad
who: Son of Jacob by Leah's servant Zilpah, ancestor of the tribe of Gad.
key: Leah named him Gad, saying good fortune had come (Genesis 30).
He went down to Egypt with Jacob and his sons (Genesis 46).

name: Gad
who: A prophet and seer in David's service who delivered the Lord's messages to the king.
key: He told David to leave the stronghold and go into the land of Judah (1 Samuel 22).
After David's census he offered the king a choice of three punishments from the Lord (2 Samuel 24).

name: Gadi
who: The father of Menahem, who seized the throne of the northern kingdom of Israel.
key: His son Menahem came up from Tirzah, killed King Shallum in Samaria, and took the throne (2 Kings 15).
Menahem son of Gadi reigned ten years in Samaria and did evil in the LORD's sight (2 Kings 15).

name: Gaham
who: A son of Nahor, Abraham's brother, by his concubine Reumah.
key: Abraham heard news of the children born to his brother Nahor (Genesis 22).
Nahor's concubine Reumah bore Tebah, Gaham, Tahash, and Maacah (Genesis 22).

name: Gaius
who: A Macedonian traveling companion of Paul who was seized during the riot in Ephesus.
key: He traveled with Paul as one of his Macedonian companions in Ephesus (Acts 19).
The rioting crowd seized him and Aristarchus and rushed together into the theater (Acts 19).

name: Gaius
who: A believer from Derbe who accompanied Paul on his journey toward Jerusalem.
key: Gaius of Derbe was among those who accompanied Paul through Macedonia toward Asia (Acts 20).
He and others went ahead and waited for Paul at Troas (Acts 20).

name: Gaius
who: A beloved believer to whom John wrote his third letter, commending his faithfulness and hospitality.
key: The elder wrote to him, rejoicing to hear that he walked in the truth (3 John 1).
He was commended for faithfully welcoming traveling brothers, even those who were strangers (3 John 1).

name: Gallio
who: The Roman proconsul of Achaia who dismissed the Jewish leaders' charges against Paul in Corinth.
key: As proconsul of Achaia, he heard Jewish leaders accuse Paul before the tribunal in Corinth (Acts 18).
He refused to judge questions about words, names, and their own law, and drove them away (Acts 18).

name: Gamaliel
who: The son of Pedahzur and chief of the tribe of Manasseh in the wilderness.
key: Named chief of the tribe of Manasseh to help Moses take the census (Numbers 1).
Led the army of Manasseh in its assigned place around the tabernacle (Numbers 2).

name: Gamaliel
who: A respected Pharisee and teacher of the law in Jerusalem, under whom Paul was educated.
key: Honored by all the people, he stood up in the council when it wanted to kill the apostles (Acts 5).
He warned that if their work was from God, the council could not overthrow it (Acts 5).

name: Gatam
who: A grandson of Esau through Eliphaz who became a chief in Edom.
key: He was a son of Eliphaz, Esau's firstborn by Adah (Genesis 36).
He is listed among the chiefs of Edom descended from Eliphaz (Genesis 36).

name: Gazez
who: A son of Caleb son of Hezron by his concubine Ephah, in the genealogy of Judah.
key: Ephah, Caleb's concubine, bore Haran, Moza, and Gazez (1 Chronicles 2).
His brother Haran also named a son Gazez (1 Chronicles 2).

name: Gedaliah
who: Son of Ahikam, appointed governor of Judah by Nebuchadnezzar after Jerusalem fell.
key: Nebuchadnezzar appointed Gedaliah governor over those left in Judah (2 Kings 25).
Jeremiah was entrusted to Gedaliah's care (Jeremiah 39; Jeremiah 40).

name: Gehazi
who: The servant of the prophet Elisha, later struck with leprosy for greedily taking gifts from Naaman.
key: He told Elisha that the Shunammite woman had no son, and later laid Elisha's staff on her dead boy (2 Kings 4).
He secretly ran after Naaman, took silver and clothing, and lied to Elisha (2 Kings 5).

name: Gemariah
who: A son of Shaphan the secretary, an official in whose chamber Baruch read Jeremiah's scroll.
key: Baruch read Jeremiah's scroll to the people from the chamber of Gemariah son of Shaphan (Jeremiah 36).
Gemariah's son Micaiah heard the words and reported them to the officials (Jeremiah 36).

name: Genubath
who: Son of Hadad the Edomite, born in Egypt and raised in Pharaoh's household.
key: He was born to Hadad the Edomite and the sister of Tahpenes, Pharaoh's queen (1 Kings 11).
Tahpenes weaned him in Pharaoh's house, where he lived among Pharaoh's sons (1 Kings 11).

name: Gera
who: A Benjaminite of Saul's clan, known as the father of Shimei, who cursed King David.
key: His son Shimei cursed David and threw stones as the king fled from Absalom (2 Samuel 16).
Shimei son of Gera later hurried to meet David and begged his pardon (2 Samuel 19).

name: Gershom
who: The firstborn son of Moses and Zipporah, born in Midian.
key: Moses named him Gershom, saying he had been a sojourner in a foreign land (Exodus 2).
Jethro brought Zipporah and her two sons to Moses in the wilderness (Exodus 18).

name: Gershon
who: The firstborn son of Levi, whose descendants the Gershonites served at the tabernacle.
key: Gershon went down to Egypt with Levi and Jacob's household (Genesis 46).
The Gershonites cared for the tabernacle's curtains, coverings, and screens (Numbers 3; Numbers 4).

name: Geshem
who: An Arab leader who joined Sanballat and Tobiah in opposing Nehemiah's rebuilding of Jerusalem.
key: With Sanballat and Tobiah, he mocked the builders and accused them of rebelling against the king (Nehemiah 2).
When the wall was nearly done, he and Sanballat invited Nehemiah to Ono, intending him harm (Nehemiah 6).

name: Gideon
who: Son of Joash and judge of Israel whom God used to deliver Israel from Midian.
key: The angel of the Lord called him while he threshed wheat in a winepress (Judges 6).
He tore down his father's Baal altar and was named Jerubbaal (Judges 6).

name: Gideoni
who: A man of the tribe of Benjamin, the father of Abidan, Benjamin's chief in the wilderness.
key: He is named as the father of Abidan, chief of Benjamin, at the census (Numbers 1).
His son Abidan led Benjamin's army west of the tabernacle (Numbers 2).

name: Gilead
who: A son of Machir and grandson of Manasseh, ancestor of the Gileadite clans of that tribe.
key: His sons headed the clans of Manasseh counted in the second census (Numbers 26).
The daughters of Zelophehad, descendants of Gilead, asked for their father's inheritance (Numbers 27).

name: Gilead
who: The father of the judge Jephthah, whose other sons drove Jephthah away.
key: He fathered Jephthah, a mighty warrior, by a prostitute (Judges 11).
His wife's sons drove Jephthah out, refusing him an inheritance in their father's house (Judges 11).

name: Gilead
who: A man of the tribe of Gad, son of Michael, listed in the Gadite genealogy.
key: He is listed among the Gadites who lived east of the Jordan in Gilead and Bashan (1 Chronicles 5).
As father of Jaroah, he was an ancestor of the Gadite family of Abihail (1 Chronicles 5).

name: God
who: The one eternal God, Creator of heaven and earth, who makes covenant with his people throughout Scripture.
key: God created the heavens, the earth, and humanity in his own image (Genesis 1).
He called Abram and promised to bless all the families of the earth through him (Genesis 12).

name: Gog
who: A Reubenite in the line of Joel, son of Shemaiah and father of Shimei.
key: The sons of Joel are traced through Shemaiah, Gog, Shimei, Micah, Reaiah, and Baal (1 Chronicles 5).
The line continued to Beerah, a Reubenite chief whom Tiglath-pileser of Assyria carried into exile (1 Chronicles 5).

name: Gog
who: Ruler from the land of Magog whom Ezekiel foresaw attacking Israel in the latter days.
key: Ezekiel prophesied against Gog, chief prince of Meshech and Tubal (Ezekiel 38).
God declared he would bring Gog against Israel in the latter years, then judge him (Ezekiel 38).

name: Goliath
who: The giant Philistine champion of Gath whom young David killed with a sling and a stone.
key: For forty days he defied the armies of Israel and challenged them to send a champion (1 Samuel 17).
David struck him with a stone from his sling and cut off his head (1 Samuel 17).

name: Gomer
who: The eldest son of Japheth, whose descendants became a people of the north.
key: He is listed first among the sons of Japheth in the table of nations (Genesis 10).
His sons Ashkenaz, Riphath, and Togarmah are named (1 Chronicles 1).

name: Gomer
who: Daughter of Diblaim and wife of the prophet Hosea, whose marriage pictured Israel's unfaithfulness to God.
key: God told Hosea to marry her, a wife of whoredom, picturing Israel forsaking the LORD (Hosea 1).
She bore Hosea a son, Jezreel, whose name announced judgment on the house of Jehu (Hosea 1).

name: Habakkuk
who: A prophet of Judah who questioned God about injustice and the coming Babylonian invasion.
key: He complained to the LORD that violence and injustice in Judah went unpunished (Habakkuk 1).
God answered that he was raising up the Chaldeans to bring judgment (Habakkuk 1).

name: Hadad
who: A king of Edom, son of Bedad, who defeated Midian in the country of Moab and reigned from Avith.
key: After Husham died, Hadad son of Bedad reigned in Edom (Genesis 36).
He defeated Midian in the country of Moab, and the name of his city was Avith (Genesis 36).

name: Hadad
who: An Edomite prince whom the Lord raised up as an adversary to Solomon.
key: As a boy he escaped to Egypt when Joab struck down the men of Edom (1 Kings 11).
Pharaoh gave him the sister of Queen Tahpenes as his wife (1 Kings 11).

name: Hadadezer
who: Son of Rehob and king of Zobah in Syria, defeated in battle by David.
key: David defeated him as he went to restore his power at the Euphrates (2 Samuel 8).
David took the gold shields of his servants to Jerusalem (2 Samuel 8).

name: Hagar
who: An Egyptian servant of Sarah who bore Abraham's son Ishmael and was twice met by the angel of the Lord.
key: Sarai gave her to Abram as a wife; when mistreated she fled, and the angel of the Lord met her (Genesis 16).
She called the Lord the God who sees her, and bore Ishmael (Genesis 16).

name: Haggai
who: A prophet to the returned exiles who urged them to finish rebuilding the temple in Jerusalem.
key: He and Zechariah prophesied to the Jews, and the rebuilding of the temple resumed (Ezra 5).
He rebuked the people for living in paneled houses while the Lord's house lay in ruins (Haggai 1).

name: Haggith
who: A wife of King David and the mother of Adonijah.
key: She bore David his fourth son, Adonijah, in Hebron (2 Samuel 3).
Her son Adonijah exalted himself and tried to take the throne (1 Kings 1).

name: Ham
who: Son of Noah who survived the flood and became ancestor of Egypt, Cush, Put, and Canaan.
key: He entered the ark with Noah and his family (Genesis 7).
He saw his father's nakedness and told his brothers, and Noah cursed Canaan (Genesis 9).

name: Haman
who: Son of Hammedatha the Agagite, a Persian official who plotted to destroy the Jews.
key: Promoted by King Ahasuerus, he plotted to kill all Jews when Mordecai would not bow (Esther 3).
On his wife's advice he built a gallows for Mordecai (Esther 5).

name: Hammedatha
who: The father of Haman the Agagite, the enemy of the Jews in Persia.
key: His son Haman was promoted above all the officials of King Ahasuerus (Esther 3).
Esther asked the king to revoke the letters devised by his son Haman (Esther 8).

name: Hamor
who: A Hivite prince of the land around Shechem and the father of Shechem, who violated Jacob's daughter Dinah.
key: Jacob bought a piece of land at Shechem from the sons of Hamor for a hundred pieces of money (Genesis 33).
After his son seized Dinah, Hamor proposed intermarriage between his people and Jacob's family (Genesis 34).

name: Hamutal
who: Daughter of Jeremiah of Libnah, wife of King Josiah, and mother of Kings Jehoahaz and Zedekiah.
key: Jehoahaz's mother was Hamutal, the daughter of Jeremiah of Libnah (2 Kings 23).
Her son Jehoahaz reigned three months before Pharaoh Neco imprisoned him (2 Kings 23).

name: Hanani
who: A seer in Judah who rebuked King Asa and was the father of the prophet Jehu.
key: His son Jehu brought the Lord's word of judgment against King Baasha of Israel (1 Kings 16).
Hanani rebuked King Asa for relying on the king of Syria instead of the Lord (2 Chronicles 16).

name: Hanani
who: A priest of the family of Immer listed among those who had married foreign women in Ezra's day.
key: The assembly in Jerusalem agreed to confess their unfaithfulness and put away their foreign wives (Ezra 10).
Hanani is listed with Zebadiah among the sons of Immer who had married foreign women (Ezra 10).

name: Hanani
who: A brother of Nehemiah who reported Jerusalem's ruin and later helped govern the city.
key: He came from Judah to Susa and told Nehemiah of Jerusalem's broken wall and burned gates (Nehemiah 1).
After the wall was finished, Nehemiah put him in charge of Jerusalem with Hananiah (Nehemiah 7).

name: Hananiah
who: A son of Shelemiah who helped repair Jerusalem's wall under Nehemiah.
key: Hananiah son of Shelemiah repaired another section of Jerusalem's wall (Nehemiah 3).
He worked on it with Hanun, the sixth son of Zalaph (Nehemiah 3).

name: Hananiah
who: The commander of Jerusalem's citadel in Nehemiah's day, known as faithful and God-fearing.
key: He commanded the citadel and was a more faithful, God-fearing man than many (Nehemiah 7).
Nehemiah put him and Hanani in charge of Jerusalem, ordering the gates guarded and kept shut (Nehemiah 7).

name: Hananiah
who: False prophet from Gibeon who opposed Jeremiah by promising a quick end to Babylon's rule.
key: In the temple he claimed God would break Babylon's yoke within two years (Jeremiah 28).
He took the yoke bars from Jeremiah's neck and broke them (Jeremiah 28).

name: Hannah
who: A wife of Elkanah whose prayer for a son was answered with the birth of the prophet Samuel.
key: Childless and provoked by Peninnah, she prayed at Shiloh and vowed to give her son to the Lord (1 Samuel 1).
Eli thought she was drunk, then blessed her, and she later bore Samuel (1 Samuel 1).

name: Hanun
who: Ammonite king, son of Nahash, who humiliated David's envoys and provoked war with Israel.
key: When he succeeded his father Nahash, David sent servants to console him (2 Samuel 10).
Suspecting spies, he shaved off half their beards and cut their garments (2 Samuel 10).

name: Hanun
who: A leader who, with the people of Zanoah, rebuilt Jerusalem's Valley Gate under Nehemiah.
key: He and the people of Zanoah rebuilt the Valley Gate and set its doors, bolts, and bars (Nehemiah 3).
They also repaired a thousand cubits of the wall, as far as the Dung Gate (Nehemiah 3).

name: Hanun
who: The sixth son of Zalaph, who helped repair Jerusalem's wall under Nehemiah.
key: He repaired another section of Jerusalem's wall during Nehemiah's rebuilding (Nehemiah 3).
He shared this work with Hananiah the son of Shelemiah (Nehemiah 3).

name: Haran
who: A son of Terah, brother of Abram and Nahor, and father of Lot, Milcah, and Iscah.
key: Haran was born to Terah, along with his brothers Abram and Nahor (Genesis 11).
He fathered Lot, as well as daughters Milcah and Iscah (Genesis 11).

name: Haran
who: A son of Caleb by his concubine Ephah, listed in the genealogy of the tribe of Judah.
key: Ephah, Caleb's concubine, bore Haran, Moza, and Gazez (1 Chronicles 2).
Haran himself fathered a son named Gazez (1 Chronicles 2).

name: Haran
who: A Gershonite Levite, son of Shimei, listed among family heads when David organized the Levites.
key: Haran is listed with Shelomoth and Haziel as the three sons of Shimei (1 Chronicles 23).
These brothers were heads of the fathers' houses of Ladan in David's organization of the Levites (1 Chronicles 23).

name: Harbona
who: A eunuch of King Ahasuerus who told the king of the gallows Haman had built for Mordecai.
key: He was one of seven eunuchs sent to bring Queen Vashti before the king (Esther 1).
He told the king that Haman had built a gallows fifty cubits high for Mordecai (Esther 7).

name: Harim
who: A priest in David's time whose family became the third of the priestly divisions and later returned from exile.
key: Harim's family received the third lot among the priestly divisions under David (1 Chronicles 24).
More than a thousand priests descended from Harim returned from Babylon with Zerubbabel (Ezra 2).

name: Harim
who: Father of Malchijah, who repaired a section of Jerusalem's wall and the Tower of the Ovens.
key: Malchijah son of Harim and Hasshub repaired a second section of the wall (Nehemiah 3).
Their work included the Tower of the Ovens (Nehemiah 3).

name: Hashabiah
who: A Levite of Merari's line who came to Ezra from Casiphia and helped carry the temple offerings to Jerusalem.
key: From Iddo's community at Casiphia came Hashabiah, with Jeshaiah of the sons of Merari (Ezra 8).
Ezra set apart Sherebiah, Hashabiah, and ten kinsmen to carry the silver, gold, and vessels (Ezra 8).

name: Hasshub
who: A descendant of Pahath-moab who repaired a section of Jerusalem's wall and the Tower of the Ovens.
key: Malchijah son of Harim and Hasshub son of Pahath-moab repaired another section and the Tower of the Ovens (Nehemiah 3).
He was one of many who rebuilt the wall section by section in Nehemiah's day (Nehemiah 3).

name: Hasshub
who: A man of Jerusalem who, with Benjamin, repaired the wall opposite his house in Nehemiah's day.
key: Benjamin and Hasshub repaired the wall opposite their house (Nehemiah 3).
After them Azariah son of Maaseiah repaired beside his own house (Nehemiah 3).

name: Hassenaah
who: Ancestor of a family whose members rebuilt Jerusalem's Fish Gate under Nehemiah.
key: His descendants rebuilt the Fish Gate, laying its beams and setting its doors, bolts, and bars (Nehemiah 3).
Next to them, Meremoth son of Uriah repaired the following section of the wall (Nehemiah 3).

name: Hathath
who: A son of Othniel, the first judge of Israel, listed in the genealogy of Judah.
key: He is named as a son of Othniel in Judah's family records (1 Chronicles 4).
He is listed alongside his brother Meonothai (1 Chronicles 4).

name: Hattush
who: A descendant of David's royal line after the exile, one of the sons of Shemaiah.
key: The sons of Shemaiah were Hattush, Igal, Bariah, Neariah, and Shaphat, six (1 Chronicles 3).
Shemaiah was the son of Shecaniah, in the royal line of Zerubbabel (1 Chronicles 3).

name: Havilah
who: A son of Cush, grandson of Ham, listed in the Table of Nations after the flood.
key: Havilah is named among the sons of Cush, alongside Seba, Sabtah, Raamah, and Sabteca (Genesis 10).
Chronicles repeats him among Cush's sons in its genealogy from Adam (1 Chronicles 1).

name: Havilah
who: A son of Joktan in Shem's line through Eber, listed in the Table of Nations.
key: Havilah is named among the thirteen sons of Joktan, with Ophir and Jobab (Genesis 10).
Chronicles repeats him among Joktan's sons in the line of Shem (1 Chronicles 1).

name: Hazael
who: An official who became king of Syria and repeatedly oppressed Israel.
key: God told Elijah to anoint Hazael king over Syria (1 Kings 19).
Elisha wept as he foretold the harm Hazael would do to Israel (2 Kings 8).

name: Haziel
who: A Gershonite Levite, son of Shimei, listed among family heads when David organized the Levites.
key: Haziel is listed with Shelomoth and Haran as the three sons of Shimei (1 Chronicles 23).
These brothers were heads of the fathers' houses of Ladan in David's organization of the Levites (1 Chronicles 23).

name: Heber
who: A grandson of Asher, son of Beriah, and ancestor of the Heberite clan.
key: He is listed among Asher's descendants who went to Egypt with Jacob (Genesis 46).
His descendants formed the clan of the Heberites in Asher (Numbers 26).

name: Heber
who: A Kenite, descended from Moses' in-law Hobab, and the husband of Jael, who killed Sisera.
key: Heber separated from the other Kenites and pitched his tent near Kedesh (Judges 4).
His household was at peace with Jabin king of Hazor (Judges 4).

name: Heber
who: A man of Judah named in Chronicles as the father, likely the founder, of the town of Soco.
key: A Judahite wife bore Jered father of Gedor, Heber father of Soco, and Jekuthiel father of Zanoah (1 Chronicles 4).
He and his brothers are listed among the clans of Judah (1 Chronicles 4).

name: Eber
who: A Gadite, one of the seven sons of Abihail who headed fathers' houses in Gilead and Bashan.
key: Abihail's sons Michael, Meshullam, Sheba, Jorai, Jacan, Zia, and Eber headed their fathers' houses (1 Chronicles 5).
These Gadites lived in Gilead, in Bashan and its towns, and in the pasturelands of Sharon (1 Chronicles 5).

name: Hebron
who: Levite son of Kohath, ancestor of the Hebronite clan that served at the tabernacle and temple.
key: He is listed as a son of Kohath, son of Levi (Exodus 6).
The Hebronites were one of the Kohathite clans serving at the tabernacle (Numbers 3).

name: Heleb
who: A warrior from Netophah, son of Baanah, counted among David's mighty men.
key: Heleb son of Baanah of Netophah is listed among David's thirty mighty men (2 Samuel 23).
Chronicles' list of David's mighty men names him Heled (1 Chronicles 11).

name: Helon
who: A man of Zebulun whose son Eliab led the tribe during Israel's wilderness journey.
key: His son Eliab was named to help Moses take the census for Zebulun (Numbers 1).
Eliab son of Helon led Zebulun's camp on the east side of the tabernacle (Numbers 2).

name: Heman
who: A famous wise man, a son of Mahol, whose wisdom Solomon surpassed; Psalm 88 bears the name Heman the Ezrahite.
key: Solomon was wiser than Ethan the Ezrahite and Heman, Calcol, and Darda, the sons of Mahol (1 Kings 4).
Psalm 88, a maskil of Heman the Ezrahite, cries out to God from deep affliction (Psalms 88).

name: Heman
who: A Levite singer of the Kohathite line, grandson of Samuel, appointed by David as a leading temple musician.
key: He is listed as a singer descended from Kohath, son of Joel and grandson of Samuel (1 Chronicles 6).
The Levites appointed him with Asaph and Ethan to sound bronze cymbals before the ark (1 Chronicles 15).

name: Hemdan
who: A Horite, son of Dishon, among the clans of Seir who lived in the land before Esau's descendants.
key: The sons of Dishon were Hemdan, Eshban, Ithran, and Cheran (Genesis 36).
Chronicles repeats these sons of Dishon among the descendants of Seir (1 Chronicles 1).

name: Hanoch
who: A son of Midian and grandson of Abraham by Keturah.
key: Midian's sons were Ephah, Epher, Hanoch, Abida, and Eldaah, all descendants of Keturah (Genesis 25).
Chronicles repeats Midian's sons, including Hanoch (1 Chronicles 1).

name: Hepher
who: A son of Gilead in the tribe of Manasseh and the grandfather of Zelophehad's five daughters.
key: Hepher was a son of Gilead and head of the Hepherite clan of Manasseh (Numbers 26).
His son Zelophehad had no sons, only five daughters (Numbers 26).

name: Herod
who: King of Judea when Jesus was born, who tried to kill the child Jesus.
key: Zechariah served as a priest in the days of Herod, king of Judea (Luke 1).
Wise men from the east came to Jerusalem asking Herod where the newborn king of the Jews was (Matthew 2).

name: Herod Antipas
who: The tetrarch of Galilee who executed John the Baptist and questioned Jesus before his crucifixion.
key: Herod imprisoned John the Baptist for condemning his marriage to Herodias (Mark 6).
At his birthday feast, he had John beheaded (Matthew 14).

name: Herod Agrippa I
who: The king, called Herod in Acts, who killed James, imprisoned Peter, and was struck down by God.
key: He killed James the brother of John with the sword (Acts 12).
Seeing it pleased the Jews, he arrested Peter during Passover (Acts 12).

name: Herodias
who: Wife of Herod Antipas, formerly married to his brother Philip, who brought about John the Baptist's death.
key: John the Baptist rebuked Herod over Herodias, his brother's wife (Luke 3).
Herod imprisoned John for her sake, and she held a grudge, wanting him killed (Mark 6).

name: Heth
who: A son of Canaan and ancestor of the Hittites, from whom Abraham bought a burial place.
key: He is listed as a son of Canaan in the table of nations (Genesis 10).
Abraham bought the cave of Machpelah from the Hittites, the descendants of Heth (Genesis 23).

name: Hezekiah
who: Faithful king of Judah, son of Ahaz, who trusted the Lord when Assyria threatened Jerusalem.
key: He removed idols and broke the bronze serpent Moses had made (2 Kings 18).
He invited all Israel to Jerusalem to keep a great Passover (2 Chronicles 30).

name: Hizkiah
who: A descendant of David's royal line after the exile, son of Neariah; not King Hezekiah.
key: He is listed as a son of Neariah, with his brothers Elioenai and Azrikam (1 Chronicles 3).
His family belongs to the line of David's descendants recorded after the exile (1 Chronicles 3).

name: Hezron
who: A son of Reuben and the founder of the Hezronite clan in the tribe of Reuben.
key: Hezron went down to Egypt with Jacob's family as one of Reuben's sons (Genesis 46).
He is listed among the heads of the fathers' houses of Reuben (Exodus 6).

name: Hezron
who: A grandson of Judah through Perez whose descendants included King David and, ultimately, Jesus.
key: He was among the family of Jacob who went down into Egypt (Genesis 46).
His descendants formed the clan of the Hezronites within the tribe of Judah (Numbers 26).

name: Hiel
who: A man of Bethel who rebuilt Jericho during King Ahab's reign, at the cost of two sons.
key: In Ahab's days Hiel of Bethel rebuilt the city of Jericho (1 Kings 16).
He laid its foundation at the cost of his firstborn Abiram, and its gates at the cost of Segub (1 Kings 16).

name: Hilkiah
who: The father of Eliakim, who was over the royal household under King Hezekiah of Judah.
key: His son Eliakim went out to meet the Assyrian field commander at Jerusalem (2 Kings 18).
Isaiah prophesied that God would call Eliakim son of Hilkiah to replace Shebna (Isaiah 22).

name: Hilkiah
who: High priest during King Josiah's reign who found the Book of the Law in the temple.
key: While the temple was being repaired, he found the Book of the Law (2 Kings 22).
He went with other officials to inquire of the prophetess Huldah (2 Kings 22).

name: Hilkiah
who: A Levite of the clan of Merari, ancestor of Ethan the singer; not the high priest Hilkiah.
key: He is listed as son of Amzi and father of Amaziah in the Merarite line (1 Chronicles 6).
His descendant Ethan was among the singers David appointed for the house of the LORD (1 Chronicles 6).

name: Hillel
who: A man of Pirathon in Ephraim, father of Abdon, who judged Israel eight years.
key: Abdon son of Hillel the Pirathonite judged Israel after Elon (Judges 12).
Abdon had forty sons and thirty grandsons who rode on seventy donkeys (Judges 12).

name: Hiram
who: King of Tyre who supplied cedar and craftsmen for David's palace and Solomon's temple.
key: Hiram sent cedar, carpenters, and masons to build David's house (2 Samuel 5).
He agreed to supply Solomon with timber for the temple (1 Kings 5).

name: Hiram
who: A skilled bronze worker from Tyre who made the bronze pillars and furnishings for Solomon's temple.
key: Solomon brought Hiram from Tyre; his mother was a widow of the tribe of Naphtali (1 Kings 7).
He cast the two bronze pillars, Jachin and Boaz, for the temple porch (1 Kings 7).

name: Hivites
label: People group
who: A Canaanite people descended from Canaan, living at Shechem, Gibeon, and beneath Mount Hermon when Israel entered the land.
key: The Hivites are listed among the descendants of Canaan in the Table of Nations (Genesis 10).
Shechem son of Hamor the Hivite violated Dinah, and Jacob's sons avenged her (Genesis 34).

name: Hobab
who: A Midianite, son of Reuel and relative of Moses by marriage, whom Moses asked to guide Israel.
key: As Israel set out from Sinai, Moses invited Hobab to come and share the LORD's good (Numbers 10).
Hobab at first declined, wishing to return to his own land and kindred (Numbers 10).

name: Hodaviah
who: A descendant of David's royal line after the exile, one of the seven sons of Elioenai.
key: The sons of Elioenai were Hodaviah, Eliashib, Pelaiah, Akkub, Johanan, Delaiah, and Anani, seven (1 Chronicles 3).
His family belonged to the royal line of Zerubbabel and King Jehoiachin (1 Chronicles 3).

name: Hodaviah
who: A Benjaminite, son of Hassenuah, whose descendant Sallu lived in Jerusalem after the exile.
key: He is listed as son of Hassenuah and father of Meshullam in a Benjaminite line (1 Chronicles 9).
His descendant Sallu son of Meshullam was among the Benjaminites living in Jerusalem (1 Chronicles 9).

name: Holy Spirit
who: The Spirit of God, the third person of the Trinity, active in creation, inspiring prophets, and indwelling believers.
key: The Spirit of God hovered over the waters at creation (Genesis 1).
The Spirit came upon judges, kings, and prophets to empower them for God's work (Judges 6).

name: Hophni
who: A son of the priest Eli who served at Shiloh and treated the Lord's offerings with contempt.
key: Hophni and his brother Phinehas served as priests of the Lord at Shiloh (1 Samuel 1).
They abused the sacrifices and ignored their father's warnings (1 Samuel 2).

name: Horam
who: A Canaanite king of Gezer defeated by Joshua during the southern campaign.
key: Horam king of Gezer came up to help Lachish while Joshua was attacking it (Joshua 10).
Joshua struck him and his people until none remained (Joshua 10).

name: Hori
who: A son of Lotan, from the Horite clans living in Seir, the land later held by Esau's descendants.
key: Hori is listed with Hemam as the sons of Lotan, whose sister was Timna (Genesis 36).
Chronicles repeats him among the descendants of Seir (1 Chronicles 1).

name: Hosea
who: A prophet to Israel's northern kingdom whose marriage to unfaithful Gomer pictured God's love for unfaithful Israel.
key: He prophesied in the days of Uzziah through Hezekiah of Judah and Jeroboam of Israel (Hosea 1).
God commanded him to marry Gomer, a picture of Israel forsaking the LORD (Hosea 1).

name: Hoshea
who: Son of Elah and last king of the northern kingdom of Israel, which fell to Assyria.
key: He conspired against King Pekah, killed him, and took the throne (2 Kings 15).
He became Assyria's vassal, then sought help from Egypt and was imprisoned (2 Kings 17).

name: Hotham
who: A man of the tribe of Asher, son of Heber and grandson of Beriah.
key: He is listed with Japhlet, Shomer, and their sister Shua as the sons of Heber (1 Chronicles 7).
Asher's descendants were heads of fathers' houses, choice men, and mighty warriors (1 Chronicles 7).

name: Huldah
who: A prophetess in Jerusalem whom King Josiah consulted after the Book of the Law was found.
key: She lived in Jerusalem's Second Quarter and was the wife of Shallum, keeper of the wardrobe (2 Kings 22).
Josiah sent Hilkiah the priest and others to her to inquire about the newly found book (2 Kings 22).

name: Hur
who: A man of Judah, son of Caleb and Ephrathah, and grandfather of Bezalel, the chief craftsman of the tabernacle.
key: The Lord chose Bezalel son of Uri, son of Hur, to make the tabernacle and its furnishings (Exodus 31).
Moses announced to Israel that the Lord had called Hur's grandson Bezalel by name (Exodus 35).

name: Hurai
who: A warrior from the brooks of Gaash, counted among David's mighty men.
key: Samuel's list of David's mighty men names him Hiddai of the brooks of Gaash (2 Samuel 23).
Chronicles' list of the same mighty men calls him Hurai (1 Chronicles 11).

name: Huri
who: A Gadite, son of Jaroah and father of Abihail, whose sons headed families in Gilead and Bashan.
key: Abihail son of Huri, son of Jaroah, is traced back to Buz in Gad's genealogy (1 Chronicles 5).
Huri's grandsons headed Gadite fathers' houses in Gilead and Bashan (1 Chronicles 5).

name: Hushai
who: An Archite and trusted friend of King David who defeated Ahithophel's counsel during Absalom's revolt.
key: When David fled Jerusalem, he sent Hushai back to frustrate Ahithophel's advice (2 Samuel 15).
Hushai greeted Absalom and offered his service, gaining access to the usurper's council (2 Samuel 16).

name: Husham
who: A man from the land of the Temanites who reigned as king of Edom before Israel had kings.
key: When Jobab died, Husham of the land of the Temanites reigned in his place (Genesis 36).
After Husham died, Hadad son of Bedad, who defeated Midian, reigned in his place (Genesis 36).

name: Hymenaeus
who: A false teacher in the church whom Paul warned Timothy about for abandoning the faith.
key: Having rejected faith and a good conscience, he made shipwreck of his faith (1 Timothy 1).
Paul handed him and Alexander over to Satan so they would learn not to blaspheme (1 Timothy 1).

name: Ibzan
who: A judge of Israel from Bethlehem who led Israel for seven years after Jephthah.
key: Ibzan of Bethlehem judged Israel after Jephthah (Judges 12).
He had thirty sons and thirty daughters, arranging marriages for them outside his clan (Judges 12).

name: Ichabod
who: Son of the priest Phinehas, named by his dying mother after the ark of God was captured.
key: His mother went into labor on hearing the ark was taken and Phinehas and Eli were dead (1 Samuel 4).
As she died, she named him Ichabod, saying the glory had departed from Israel (1 Samuel 4).

name: Iddo
who: A priest who returned from exile, the grandfather of the prophet Zechariah.
key: An Iddo is listed among the priests who came up from exile with Zerubbabel (Nehemiah 12).
Ezra calls the prophet Zechariah his son, naming him by his grandfather (Ezra 5).

name: Iddo
who: The leader at Casiphia in Babylonia, to whom Ezra sent for Levites to serve the temple.
key: Finding no Levites among the returnees, Ezra sent men to Iddo, the leading man at Casiphia (Ezra 8).
Iddo's community sent Sherebiah, Hashabiah, and Jeshaiah with other Levites (Ezra 8).

name: Igal
who: Son of Joseph of Issachar, one of the twelve spies Moses sent to explore Canaan.
key: Moses sent Igal son of Joseph to represent Issachar among the twelve spies (Numbers 13).
He was among the spies who brought back a bad report of the land (Numbers 13).

name: Igal
who: A warrior from Zobah, son of Nathan, counted among David's mighty men.
key: Igal son of Nathan of Zobah is listed among David's thirty mighty men (2 Samuel 23).
Zobah was an Aramean kingdom that David had earlier defeated (2 Samuel 8).

name: Igal
who: A descendant of David's royal line after the exile, one of the sons of Shemaiah.
key: The sons of Shemaiah were Hattush, Igal, Bariah, Neariah, and Shaphat, six (1 Chronicles 3).
Shemaiah was the son of Shecaniah, in the royal line of Zerubbabel (1 Chronicles 3).

name: Immer
who: A priest named as an ancestor of priests who lived and served in Jerusalem after the exile.
key: Immer is named in the ancestry of Maasai, a priest who lived in Jerusalem after the exile (1 Chronicles 9).
Nehemiah's list traces the priest Amashsai back through Meshillemoth to Immer (Nehemiah 11).

name: Immer
who: A priest whose family became the sixteenth priestly division and returned from exile in Babylon.
key: Immer's family drew the sixteenth lot among the priestly divisions under David (1 Chronicles 24).
More than a thousand priests of Immer's line returned from Babylon with Zerubbabel (Ezra 2).

name: Imnah
who: A son of Asher and grandson of Jacob, ancestor of the clan of the Imnites.
key: Imnah is listed first among the sons of Asher who went down to Egypt with Jacob (Genesis 46).
From Imnah came the clan of the Imnites in the census on the plains of Moab (Numbers 26).

name: Irad
who: A descendant of Cain, son of Enoch and father of Mehujael.
key: Irad was born to Enoch, the son of Cain after whom Cain named his city (Genesis 4).
Irad fathered Mehujael, continuing Cain's line toward Lamech (Genesis 4).

name: Iru
who: A son of Caleb son of Jephunneh, listed in the genealogy of Judah.
key: Iru is named first among the sons of Caleb son of Jephunneh, with Elah and Naam (1 Chronicles 4).
His brother Elah was the father of Kenaz (1 Chronicles 4).

name: Isaac
who: The promised son of Abraham and Sarah, father of Jacob and Esau, and heir of God's covenant.
key: He was born to Abraham and Sarah in their old age, as God had promised (Genesis 21).
Abraham bound him on an altar, but God provided a ram in his place (Genesis 22).

name: Isaiah
who: Son of Amoz and prophet in Jerusalem who foretold judgment and the coming Messiah.
key: He saw the Lord enthroned in the temple and was sent to prophesy (Isaiah 6).
He gave King Ahaz the sign of a virgin bearing a son, Immanuel (Isaiah 7).

name: Iscah
who: A daughter of Haran, niece of Abram, and sister of Lot and Milcah.
key: She was a daughter of Haran, Abram's brother, who died in Ur (Genesis 11).
She is named when her uncle Nahor married her sister Milcah (Genesis 11).

name: Ish-bosheth
who: A son of Saul whom Abner made king over Israel for two years after Saul's death.
key: Abner made him king over Israel while Judah followed David (2 Samuel 2).
He accused Abner over Saul's concubine, and Abner turned to support David (2 Samuel 3).

name: Ishbak
who: A son of Abraham by Keturah, sent away eastward with his brothers.
key: Keturah bore Abraham Zimran, Jokshan, Medan, Midian, Ishbak, and Shuah (Genesis 25).
Abraham gave gifts to his concubines' sons and sent them east, away from Isaac (Genesis 25).

name: Ishbi-benob
who: A Philistine warrior descended from the giants who tried to kill David in battle.
key: Armed with a new sword and a heavy bronze spear, he thought to kill a weary David (2 Samuel 21).
Abishai son of Zeruiah came to David's aid and killed him (2 Samuel 21).

name: Ishmael
who: Son of Abraham by Hagar the Egyptian, and father of twelve tribal princes.
key: The angel of the LORD told Hagar to name her son Ishmael (Genesis 16).
He was circumcised at thirteen, and God promised to make him a great nation (Genesis 17).

name: Ishmael
who: Son of Nethaniah, of the royal family of Judah, who murdered the governor Gedaliah.
key: Johanan warned Gedaliah that the Ammonite king had sent Ishmael to kill him (Jeremiah 40).
Ishmael killed Gedaliah and others at Mizpah (Jeremiah 41).

name: Ishmael
who: The father of Zebadiah, governor of the house of Judah under King Jehoshaphat.
key: Jehoshaphat set Zebadiah son of Ishmael over all the king's matters (2 Chronicles 19).
Zebadiah served as governor of the house of Judah beside Amariah the chief priest (2 Chronicles 19).

name: Ispah
who: A Benjaminite, son of Beriah, named among the family heads of Benjamin who lived in Jerusalem.
key: Michael, Ispah, and Joha are named among the sons of Beriah (1 Chronicles 8).
Beriah and Shema, heads in Aijalon, had put the inhabitants of Gath to flight (1 Chronicles 8).

name: Jacob
who: Son of Isaac and Rebekah, renamed Israel by God, whose twelve sons became the tribes of Israel.
key: He was born holding Esau's heel and later bought Esau's birthright for stew (Genesis 25).
He deceived his blind father Isaac to receive the blessing meant for Esau (Genesis 27).

name: Issachar
who: Jacob's fifth son by Leah and ancestor of the tribe of Issachar.
key: Leah bore Issachar after giving Rachel her son's mandrakes (Genesis 30).
He went down to Egypt with his four sons (Genesis 46).

name: Ithamar
who: Youngest son of Aaron, ordained as a priest and overseer of Levite duties at the tabernacle.
key: He was set apart with his father and brothers to serve as a priest (Exodus 28).
He directed the Levites' accounting of the materials used for the tabernacle (Exodus 38).

name: Ithiel
who: A Benjaminite, son of Jeshaiah and father of Maaseiah, in the ancestry of Sallu of Jerusalem.
key: Sallu son of Meshullam is traced through Joed, Pedaiah, Kolaiah, Maaseiah, and Ithiel to Jeshaiah (Nehemiah 11).
These Benjaminites were among the people who lived in Jerusalem, the holy city (Nehemiah 11).

name: Ithran
who: A Horite, son of Dishon, among the clans of Seir who lived in the land before Esau's descendants.
key: The sons of Dishon were Hemdan, Eshban, Ithran, and Cheran (Genesis 36).
Chronicles repeats these sons of Dishon among the descendants of Seir (1 Chronicles 1).

name: Ittai
who: Ittai the Gittite, a foreigner from Gath who stayed loyal to David during Absalom's rebellion.
key: David urged him to return home, but he vowed to stay with David in life or death (2 Samuel 15).
He crossed the Kidron with his men and their little ones (2 Samuel 15).

name: Izhar
who: Levite son of Kohath and father of Korah, ancestor of the Izharite clan.
key: He is listed as a son of Kohath, with sons Korah, Nepheg, and Zichri (Exodus 6).
The Izharites were one of the Kohathite clans serving at the tabernacle (Numbers 3).

name: Jaazaniah
who: A Rechabite, son of Jeremiah, whose family kept their ancestor's command to drink no wine.
key: Jeremiah brought Jaazaniah and the whole house of the Rechabites into a temple chamber (Jeremiah 35).
Offered wine, they refused, citing the command of their ancestor Jonadab son of Rechab (Jeremiah 35).

name: Jabal
who: A son of Lamech and Adah, the father of those who live in tents and keep livestock.
key: Adah bore Jabal to Lamech, a descendant of Cain (Genesis 4).
He was the father of those who dwell in tents and have livestock (Genesis 4).

name: Jabesh
who: The father of Shallum, who killed King Zechariah of Israel and reigned one month.
key: Shallum son of Jabesh conspired against King Zechariah, killed him, and reigned in his place (2 Kings 15).
Shallum son of Jabesh reigned one month in Samaria (2 Kings 15).

name: Jabez
who: A man listed among Judah's descendants, more honorable than his brothers, whose prayer God answered.
key: He was more honorable than his brothers, and his mother named him for bearing him in pain (1 Chronicles 4).
He called on God to bless him, enlarge his border, and keep him from harm (1 Chronicles 4).

name: Jabin
who: A Canaanite king of Hazor who led the northern kings against Joshua and was killed.
key: Hearing of Israel's victories, Jabin summoned the kings of the north to fight Israel (Joshua 11).
Their great army, with many horses and chariots, camped at the waters of Merom (Joshua 11).

name: Jabin
who: A king of Canaan reigning in Hazor who oppressed Israel in the days of Deborah.
key: The Lord sold Israel into his hand, and he oppressed them twenty years (Judges 4).
His commander Sisera led nine hundred chariots of iron (Judges 4).

name: Jacob
who: Son of Matthan and father of Joseph, Mary's husband, in Matthew's genealogy of Jesus; not the patriarch.
key: Matthew lists him as son of Matthan in the royal line descended from David (Matthew 1).
He was the father of Joseph, the husband of Mary, of whom Jesus was born (Matthew 1).

name: Jada
who: A man of Judah in the line of Jerahmeel, son of Onam and father of Jether and Jonathan.
key: Jada and his brother Shammai are listed as the sons of Onam (1 Chronicles 2).
Jada's sons were Jether and Jonathan; Jether died without children (1 Chronicles 2).

name: Jaddua
who: A high priest after the exile, the last in the line of high priests listed in Nehemiah.
key: The high-priestly line runs from Jeshua through Joiakim, Eliashib, Joiada, and Jonathan to Jaddua (Nehemiah 12).
Levite family heads were recorded in the days of Eliashib, Joiada, Johanan, and Jaddua (Nehemiah 12).

name: Jael
who: The wife of Heber the Kenite, who killed the Canaanite commander Sisera in her tent.
key: Sisera fled to her tent, since Jabin was at peace with Heber's house (Judges 4).
She gave him milk, covered him, and drove a tent peg through his temple (Judges 4).

name: Jahaziel
who: A Levite of the clan of Kohath, the third son of Hebron.
key: He is listed as Hebron's third son in David's organization of the Levites (1 Chronicles 23).
His name appears again among the Levite families assigned by lot for service (1 Chronicles 24).

name: Jahaziel
who: A Levite of the sons of Asaph who prophesied victory to King Jehoshaphat facing a vast invading army.
key: As Judah gathered to pray, the Spirit of the LORD came upon Jahaziel in the assembly (2 Chronicles 20).
He told them not to fear, for the battle was not theirs but God's (2 Chronicles 20).

name: Jahdai
who: A man of Judah listed among Caleb's descendants, whose six sons are named in Chronicles.
key: His sons were Regem, Jotham, Geshan, Pelet, Ephah, and Shaaph (1 Chronicles 2).
He appears in the genealogy of Caleb within the tribe of Judah (1 Chronicles 2).

name: Jair
who: The father of Elhanan, the warrior who killed Lahmi, the brother of Goliath.
key: Elhanan son of Jair struck down Lahmi, the brother of Goliath the Gittite (1 Chronicles 20).
Samuel's parallel account calls Elhanan's father Jaare-oregim the Bethlehemite (2 Samuel 21).

name: Jair
who: A descendant of Manasseh who captured villages east of the Jordan and named them Havvoth-jair.
key: Jair son of Manasseh captured villages in Gilead and called them Havvoth-jair (Numbers 32).
He took the whole region of Argob in Bashan and named it after himself (Deuteronomy 3).

name: Jair
who: A Gileadite who judged Israel for twenty-two years after Tola.
key: After Tola, Jair the Gileadite judged Israel twenty-two years (Judges 10).
His thirty sons rode thirty donkeys and had thirty cities in Gilead called Havvoth-jair (Judges 10).

name: Jairus
who: A synagogue ruler whose twelve-year-old daughter Jesus raised from the dead.
key: Jairus fell at Jesus' feet, begging him to come heal his dying daughter (Mark 5).
On the way, Jesus stopped to speak with a woman healed of a bleeding disorder (Mark 5).

name: Jakeh
who: The father of Agur, whose wise sayings are collected in the book of Proverbs.
key: Proverbs 30 opens with the words of Agur son of Jakeh (Proverbs 30).
Jakeh's son confesses his weariness and limited understanding before God (Proverbs 30).

name: James
who: Apostle of Jesus, son of Zebedee and brother of John, who was martyred by Herod.
key: Jesus called him and John from mending nets with their father (Matthew 4).
He was appointed one of the Twelve, and Jesus called the brothers Boanerges (Mark 3).

name: James
who: The son of Alphaeus and one of the twelve apostles chosen by Jesus.
key: Jesus named James son of Alphaeus among the twelve apostles he sent out (Matthew 10).
Mark lists him among the Twelve appointed to preach and cast out demons (Mark 3).

name: James
who: Brother of Jesus who became a leader of the Jerusalem church and wrote the letter of James.
key: He is named among Jesus' brothers by the people of Nazareth (Matthew 13).
Peter sent word to him after being freed from prison (Acts 12).

name: Jamin
who: A man of Judah, son of Ram and grandson of Jerahmeel.
key: Ram was the firstborn son of Jerahmeel (1 Chronicles 2).
The sons of Ram were Maaz, Jamin, and Eker (1 Chronicles 2).

name: Japheth
who: One of Noah's three sons, who survived the flood in the ark and became ancestor of many nations.
key: He is named as a son of Noah, along with Shem and Ham (Genesis 5).
He entered the ark with his wife, his parents, and his brothers (Genesis 7).

name: Japhlet
who: A man of the tribe of Asher, son of Heber and grandson of Beriah.
key: He is listed with Shomer, Hotham, and their sister Shua as the sons of Heber (1 Chronicles 7).
His sons were Pasach, Bimhal, and Ashvath (1 Chronicles 7).

name: Jarah
who: A descendant of King Saul through Jonathan, son of Ahaz, in the genealogy of Benjamin.
key: The first list of Saul's line calls him Jehoaddah son of Ahaz (1 Chronicles 8).
In the repeated genealogy, Ahaz fathered Jarah (1 Chronicles 9).

name: Jared
who: A son of Mahalalel and father of Enoch in the line from Adam to Noah.
key: He was born when his father Mahalalel was sixty-five (Genesis 5).
He fathered Enoch at 162 and lived 962 years (Genesis 5).

name: Jaroah
who: A man of the tribe of Gad, son of Gilead, listed in the Gadite genealogy.
key: Jaroah is named as the son of Gilead and the father of Huri among the Gadites (1 Chronicles 5).
Through Huri he was an ancestor of Abihail, whose sons lived in Gilead and Bashan (1 Chronicles 5).

name: Jason
who: A believer in Thessalonica who hosted Paul and Silas and was dragged before the city authorities.
key: A mob attacked Jason's house while searching for Paul and Silas (Acts 17).
They dragged Jason before the city authorities, accusing him of harboring the missionaries (Acts 17).

name: Javan
who: A son of Japheth whose descendants became coastland peoples; his name later designates Greece.
key: He is listed among the sons of Japheth, with sons Elishah, Tarshish, Kittim, and Dodanim (Genesis 10).
Chronicles repeats his line among Japheth's descendants (1 Chronicles 1).

name: Jebusites
label: People group
who: A Canaanite people who held Jerusalem, then called Jebus, until David captured it.
key: The Jebusites are listed among the peoples descended from Canaan (Genesis 10).
The people of Judah could not drive out the Jebusites living in Jerusalem (Joshua 15).

name: Jediael
who: A son of Benjamin whose descendants through Bilhan were mighty warriors and heads of fathers' houses.
key: The sons of Benjamin were Bela, Becher, and Jediael, three (1 Chronicles 7).
Jediael's son was Bilhan, whose seven sons are named (1 Chronicles 7).

name: Jeduthun
who: A Levite musician appointed by David to lead praise and thanksgiving to the Lord with lyres and other instruments.
key: He was appointed with Heman to give thanks to the Lord before the tabernacle at Gibeon (1 Chronicles 16).
David set apart his sons to prophesy with lyres in thanksgiving and praise (1 Chronicles 25).

name: Jehiel
who: A Gershonite Levite, chief of the sons of Ladan, whose family oversaw the temple treasuries.
key: He is named chief among the sons of Ladan in David's organization of the Levites (1 Chronicles 23).
His family was put in charge of the treasuries of the house of the LORD (1 Chronicles 26).

name: Jehoahaz
who: Son of Josiah who reigned three months over Judah before Pharaoh Neco deposed him and took him to Egypt.
key: The people of the land made him king after Josiah's death (2 Kings 23).
He did evil and reigned three months before Pharaoh Neco imprisoned him at Riblah (2 Kings 23).

name: Jehoahaz
who: King of Israel, son of Jehu, who reigned seventeen years in Samaria.
key: He succeeded his father Jehu as king of Israel (2 Kings 10).
He did evil, so the LORD gave Israel into the hand of Hazael of Syria (2 Kings 13).

name: Jehoiachin
who: King of Judah who reigned three months before being taken captive to Babylon by Nebuchadnezzar.
key: He became king at eighteen and did evil in the sight of the LORD (2 Kings 24).
He surrendered to Nebuchadnezzar and was exiled to Babylon with his family and officials (2 Kings 24).

name: Jehoiada
who: Father of Benaiah, the valiant man from Kabzeel who commanded David's bodyguard and later Solomon's army.
key: His son Benaiah was placed over David's Cherethites and Pelethites (2 Samuel 8).
A Jehoiada led 3,700 men of the house of Aaron to David at Hebron (1 Chronicles 12).

name: Jehoiada
who: The priest who protected the boy Joash and restored the line of David to Judah's throne.
key: He and his wife hid Joash in the temple for six years (2 Chronicles 22).
He crowned Joash king and had Athaliah put to death (2 Kings 11).

name: Jehoiada
who: Son of Benaiah, one of King David's counselors after Ahithophel.
key: Jehoiada son of Benaiah succeeded Ahithophel as a counselor to King David (1 Chronicles 27).
He served alongside Abiathar, while Joab commanded the king's army (1 Chronicles 27).

name: Jehoiakim
who: A son of Josiah whom Pharaoh Neco made king of Judah, and who opposed Jeremiah.
key: Pharaoh Neco made Eliakim king and changed his name to Jehoiakim (2 Kings 23).
He taxed the land heavily to pay the tribute Egypt demanded (2 Kings 23).

name: Jehoram
who: King of Judah, son of Jehoshaphat, who married Ahab's daughter and followed the ways of Israel's kings.
key: When he became king, he killed all his brothers with the sword (2 Chronicles 21).
He walked in the way of Ahab's house, for Ahab's daughter was his wife (2 Kings 8).

name: Jehosheba
who: A daughter of King Jehoram and wife of the priest Jehoiada, who saved young Joash from Athaliah.
key: When Athaliah destroyed the royal family, Jehosheba stole away her nephew Joash, son of Ahaziah (2 Kings 11).
She hid him and his nurse in a bedroom so he was not killed (2 Kings 11).

name: Jehoshaphat
who: Son of Ahilud, the royal recorder under King David and King Solomon.
key: Jehoshaphat son of Ahilud served as recorder among David's officials (2 Samuel 8).
He is again listed as recorder after David's return to Jerusalem (2 Samuel 20).

name: Jehoshaphat
who: Son of Paruah, one of King Solomon's twelve district officers, over Issachar.
key: Solomon's twelve officers each supplied food for the king's household one month a year (1 Kings 4).
Jehoshaphat son of Paruah served as the officer over Issachar (1 Kings 4).

name: Jehoshaphat
who: Son of Asa and a godly king of Judah who sought the Lord and taught his law.
key: He sent officials and Levites to teach the Book of the Law in Judah (2 Chronicles 17).
He allied with Ahab at Ramoth-gilead and narrowly escaped death (1 Kings 22).

name: Jehoshaphat
who: Son of Nimshi and father of Jehu, who became king of Israel.
key: Elisha sent a young prophet to anoint Jehu son of Jehoshaphat, son of Nimshi (2 Kings 9).
His son Jehu conspired against King Joram and seized Israel's throne (2 Kings 9).

name: Jehu
who: A prophet, son of Hanani the seer, who announced judgment on King Baasha and rebuked King Jehoshaphat.
key: Jehu announced that the Lord would sweep away Baasha's house for his sins (1 Kings 16).
Zimri destroyed Baasha's whole house, fulfilling the word spoken through Jehu (1 Kings 16).

name: Jehu
who: Army commander anointed king of Israel to destroy the house of Ahab and Baal worship.
key: God told Elijah to anoint Jehu king over Israel (1 Kings 19).
Anointed by a young prophet sent by Elisha, he killed Kings Joram and Ahaziah (2 Kings 9).

name: Jekameam
who: A Levite of the clan of Kohath, the fourth son of Hebron.
key: He is listed as Hebron's fourth son in David's organization of the Levites (1 Chronicles 23).
His name appears again among the Levite families assigned by lot for service (1 Chronicles 24).

name: Jekuthiel
who: A man of Judah, listed in Chronicles as the father, likely the founder, of the town of Zanoah.
key: Chronicles names Jered, Heber, and Jekuthiel as sons borne by a Judahite wife (1 Chronicles 4).
Jekuthiel is called the father of Zanoah, a town of Judah (1 Chronicles 4).

name: Jephthah
who: A Gileadite warrior who judged Israel six years after defeating the Ammonites.
key: Driven out by his half-brothers, Jephthah was later recalled to lead Gilead (Judges 11).
He vowed an offering to the Lord and defeated the Ammonites (Judges 11).

name: Jephunneh
who: Kenizzite of the tribe of Judah, known as the father of Caleb, one of the two faithful spies.
key: His son Caleb represented Judah among the twelve spies sent into Canaan (Numbers 13).
The LORD promised that Caleb son of Jephunneh would enter the land (Numbers 14).

name: Jerahmeel
who: The firstborn son of Hezron of Judah, whose descendants are listed in Chronicles.
key: He is named first among the sons of Hezron (1 Chronicles 2).
His sons were Ram, Bunah, Oren, Ozem, and Ahijah (1 Chronicles 2).

name: Jerahmeel
who: A Merarite Levite, son of Kish, who headed a family in David's Levite divisions.
key: Jerahmeel is listed as the son of Kish among the Merarite Levites (1 Chronicles 24).
These Levites cast lots before King David, Zadok, and Ahimelech, as their priestly brothers did (1 Chronicles 24).

name: Jered
who: A man of Judah named in Chronicles as the father, likely the founder, of the town of Gedor.
key: A Judahite wife bore Jered father of Gedor, Heber father of Soco, and Jekuthiel father of Zanoah (1 Chronicles 4).
He and his brothers are listed among the clans of Judah (1 Chronicles 4).

name: Jeremiah
who: A man of Libnah, grandfather of Kings Jehoahaz and Zedekiah through his daughter Hamutal; not the prophet.
key: His daughter Hamutal was the mother of King Jehoahaz of Judah (2 Kings 23).
Hamutal was also the mother of Zedekiah, Judah's last king (2 Kings 24).

name: Jeremiah
who: Prophet from a priestly family who warned Judah of judgment before and during Babylon's conquest of Jerusalem.
key: God called him as a prophet while he was still young (Jeremiah 1).
Pashhur the priest beat him and put him in the stocks (Jeremiah 20).

name: Jeremiah
who: A Rechabite, son of Habazziniah and father of Jaazaniah; not the prophet Jeremiah.
key: The prophet Jeremiah brought his son Jaazaniah and the Rechabites into the temple and offered them wine (Jeremiah 35).
They refused, obeying their ancestor Jonadab, and the LORD promised their line would endure (Jeremiah 35).

name: Jeremoth
who: A Levite of the clan of Merari, son of Mushi.
key: He is listed with Mahli and Eder as the sons of Mushi in David's Levite organization (1 Chronicles 23).
His name appears again among the Levite families assigned by lot for service (1 Chronicles 24).

name: Jeriah
who: A Levite of the clan of Kohath, the chief among the sons of Hebron.
key: He is listed as the chief of Hebron's sons in David's organization of the Levites (1 Chronicles 23).
His name appears again among the Levite families assigned by lot for service (1 Chronicles 24).

name: Jerimoth
who: A son of David whose daughter Mahalath became a wife of King Rehoboam.
key: Rehoboam took as wife Mahalath, the daughter of Jerimoth son of David (2 Chronicles 11).
Mahalath bore Rehoboam three sons, Jeush, Shemariah, and Zaham (2 Chronicles 11).

name: Jeroboam
who: Son of Nebat and first king of the northern kingdom of Israel, who led it into idolatry.
key: The prophet Ahijah tore his cloak and promised Jeroboam ten tribes (1 Kings 11).
When the northern tribes rejected Rehoboam, they made Jeroboam king (1 Kings 12).

name: Jeroboam
who: King of Israel, son of Joash, who restored Israel's borders; often called Jeroboam II.
key: He reigned forty-one years in Samaria and did evil in the LORD's sight (2 Kings 14).
He restored Israel's border as the LORD spoke through Jonah (2 Kings 14).
